abstract: OpenAI has claimed that the Riemann zeta function has no zeros with real part greater than 7/8. The claim has not been refereed, and every result here assumes it. Visser showed that it implies a prime in (x, x + x^{7/8}) for every x > 1, and hence a prime between n^8 and (n+1)^8 for every n. The gap (n+1)^7 - n^7 is about 7x^{6/7} with x = n^7, which is shorter than x^{7/8}, so Visser's argument does not reach seventh powers. We combine the half-plane with the explicit zero-density estimate of Fiori, Kadiri and Swidinsky and the explicit formula of Cully-Hugill and Johnston. The sum over zeros in the explicit formula is then bounded by a fixed negative power of x whenever the interval has length x^θ with θ > 5/8. We prove that, if ζ(s) ≠ 0 for Re s > 7/8, there is a prime between n^7 and (n+1)^7 for every n ≥ 1. The proof splits the range: n ≤ 200 directly; 37 ≤ log x ≤ 260 with the conditional bounds for ψ(x) of Fiori and Jaskari; 244 ≤ log x ≤ 10^6 with the explicit formula and the density estimate, checked on 1302 intervals with smallest margin 0.138; and log x ≥ 10^6 analytically. For m = 6, 5, 4, 3 the same method gives a prime between n^m and (n+1)^m once log(n^m) ≥ 285, 366, 575 and 2203 respectively. Unconditionally the best result for all n is m = 86 (Lee). The supplement contains the scripts and their outputs.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary: Revised after the review of version 1. No theorem, threshold or interval cover changed. (1) New Lemma 7 states explicit majorants F, G for the tail log x >= 10^6, with derivative bounds showing they decrease; Sections 5.4 and 6 now use it. A new script tail_majorant.py evaluates them in interval arithmetic. The tail margins in Section 6 are restated as these conservative lower bounds (0.99994-0.99997); the m = 7 tail bound is stated as at least 0.99997 (computed 0.9999782) instead of the rounded-up 0.99998. (2) Proposition 6 now requires h > 0. (3) psi, theta and Lambda are defined on first use. (4) The classical argument is credited to Ingham (1937). (5) References are numbered. (6) Package versions are recorded in Section 8 and the supplement README.
title: Primes between consecutive seventh powers, assuming the claimed 7/8 zero-free half-plane
